routing.notes: The router assigns causal_type_id/theory_id before reasoning. The reasoner also receives anchor norms from the causality type and then uses retrieval for substantive norms (supportive/neutral).

few_shot_examples.claim: The seller did not deliver the property within the time specified in the contract and is still asking for the balance.
The creditor is taking action after many years and I fear the right is time-barred.
I was robbed at home and I want to file a complaint.
The Municipality does not respond to my request for access to documents within the procedural deadlines.

core_norms.role: Basis of the link between conduct (action/omission) -> event

accessory_norms.role: Concurrence of causes and supervening causes, to be read systematically with Art. 40 c.p.
Subjective element (fault/intent). Relevant for negligent causality, does not define the link itself

principle_tests.name: Conditio sine qua non (counterfactual)
principle_tests.description: If by mentally eliminating the conduct the event does not occur, the conduct is a condition of the event

principle_tests.name: Covering law (scientific-probabilistic when necessary)
principle_tests.description: When the link is not deterministic, a scientific/empirical rule is used to support the counterfactual

core_norms.role: Concurrence of causes and interruption of the link by a sole sufficient supervening cause

accessory_norms.role: Basis of the link, read systematically with Art. 41 c.p.
Foreseeability/fault: useful for assessing the relevance of the supervening cause in a negligent act
Fortuitous event/force majeure: filter on imputation/punishability
Irrelevance of emotional/passionate states on imputability

principle_tests.name: Equivalence of conditions (41.1)
principle_tests.description: Concurrent causes do not exclude the link if the conduct remains a condition of the event

principle_tests.name: Sole sufficient supervening cause (41.2)
principle_tests.description: A supervening cause breaks the link if it is independently sufficient to produce the event

accessory_norms.role: Foreseeability of damage (if there is no intent)

principle_tests.name: Immediate and direct consequence
principle_tests.description: Selects only non-mediated/atypical damages with respect to the breach/tort

principle_tests.name: Ex ante foreseeability
principle_tests.description: Excludes damages not foreseeable at the time of the obligation (except for intent)

principle_tests.name: Mitigation/creditor's contribution
principle_tests.description: Reduces or excludes avoidable or concurrent damages due to the creditor's conduct

core_norms.role: General principles of administrative action (economy, impartiality, transparency)
Obligation to conclude the procedure and regulation of deadline/silence
Obligation to state reasons for the administrative act

accessory_norms.role: Communication of the start of the procedure and participatory guarantees
Notice of rejection and procedural cross-examination
Annullability of the act and invalidating relevance of procedural defects
Right of access to administrative documents

principle_tests.name: Procedural deadlines and silence
principle_tests.description: Verifies compliance with conclusion deadlines, inertia, and correct regulation of administrative silence

principle_tests.name: Adequacy of the motivation
principle_tests.description: Checks the existence, completeness, and coherence of the motivation with respect to the facts and the applied norms

principle_tests.name: Participatory guarantees and cross-examination
principle_tests.description: Verifies the effectiveness of procedural participation (initiation, notice of rejection, access)

principle_tests.name: Invalidating effect of the defect
principle_tests.description: Assesses whether the procedural defect is concretely capable of affecting the content of the act (art. 21-octies)

accessory_norms.role: Sole sufficient supervening cause: systematic junction close to fortuitous event
State of necessity as a possible alternative filter for non-punishability
Excludes that the mere emotional state constitutes a fortuitous event/force majeure

principle_tests.name: Unforeseeable and unavoidable
principle_tests.description: Uncontrollable external event that prevents imputation

core_norms.role: Termination for breach and cumulation with damages

principle_tests.name: Seriousness of the breach
principle_tests.description: Verifies if the breach exceeds the threshold of non-trivial importance

principle_tests.name: Compatibility between remedies
principle_tests.description: Checks compatibility and limits between termination, deposit, penalty, and damages

causal_types.name: Warranty for defects and remedies in sales (civil)

core_norms.role: Warranty for defects of the sold item

principle_tests.name: Proof of the relevant defect
principle_tests.description: Ascertains the existence, seriousness, and functional impact of the reported defect

principle_tests.name: Timeliness of the report
principle_tests.description: Verifies forfeiture and prescription for the warranty action

causal_types.name: Liability for custody and damage from things/animals (civil)

core_norms.role: Damage caused by a thing in custody

accessory_norms.role: Contribution of the injured party and mitigation

principle_tests.name: Thing/animal-damage link
principle_tests.description: Verifies the causal link between the source in custody and the harmful event

principle_tests.name: Fortuitous event and contribution
principle_tests.description: Assesses external fortuitous event and the impact of the injured party's behavior

principle_tests.name: Offence boundaries
principle_tests.description: Checks boundaries between contiguous property offences

principle_tests.name: Proof of the subjective element
principle_tests.description: Verifies proof of specific intent or unjust profit required

core_norms.role: Exercise of a right / fulfillment of a duty

accessory_norms.role: Arbitrary exercise of one's own rights
Violence against things or persons in self-help

principle_tests.name: Balancing of opposing rights
principle_tests.description: Balances reputation/freedom of expression or credit/self-help and penal limits

principle_tests.name: Scope of the justification
principle_tests.description: Assesses whether the justification fully covers the contested conduct

accessory_norms.role: Severity of the crime and sentencing
Irrelevance of emotional/passionate states on imputability
State of necessity as a possible justification/mitigation to be assessed in the context of urgency

principle_tests.name: Blameworthiness scale
principle_tests.description: Assesses the degree of fault, foreseeability, and avoidability in practice

principle_tests.name: Individualization of liability
principle_tests.description: Distinguishes individual contributions in multi-subject negligent acts

core_norms.role: Ex officio annulment and time limits/reliance
Revocation for supervening events and indemnity

principle_tests.name: Current public interest
principle_tests.description: Verifies the concreteness and timeliness of the public interest in self-protection

principle_tests.name: Reliance balancing
principle_tests.description: Assesses the sacrifice imposed on the private party and the protection of consolidated reliance

core_norms.role: Obligation to conclude the procedure within the deadlines

principle_tests.name: Breach of deadlines
principle_tests.description: Ascertains exceeding the procedural deadline and the imputability of the delay

principle_tests.name: Proof of damage from delay
principle_tests.description: Verifies proof of consequential damage and the causal link with the delay

causal_types.name: Concurrence between penal and civil protection (mixed)

core_norms.role: Restitution and compensation for damage from crime

accessory_norms.role: Compensable damages for immediate and direct consequences

principle_tests.name: Autonomy of tracks
principle_tests.description: Distinguishes penal assessment from civil prerequisites and remedies

principle_tests.name: Cumulability limits
principle_tests.description: Verifies limits and conditions of the cumulation of civil claims and penal profiles

theories.name: Interruption by a sole sufficient supervening cause
Procedural guarantees and validity of the administrative act
Contractual remedies and rebalancing of the synallagma
Warranty for defects and limits of construction/commercial remedies
Liability for custody and causal contribution
Property offences and evidentiary threshold of the subjective element
Balancing between fundamental rights and penal typicality
Gradation of fault and individualization of blame
Procedural delay and proof of consequential damage
Concurrence between penal claims and civil remedies

but_for_fails.description: Counterfactual fails: the event would have occurred anyway.

no_covering_law_or_low_support.description: Missing covering law or insufficient support for probabilistic counterfactual.

alternative_causal_path.description: A plausible alternative causal path exists.

duty_to_act_missing_for_omission.description: For omission, the legal duty to act is missing.

abnormal_or_atypical_chain.description: The causal chain is abnormal/atypical and breaks imputability.

sole_sufficient_cause.description: A supervening cause alone was sufficient and breaks the link.

intervening_cause_breaks_chain.description: An intervening autonomous factor breaks the chain.

damage_is_indirect.description: The damage is indirect or mediated relative to the base fact.

damage_not_foreseeable.description: The damage was not foreseeable ex ante (e.g., art. 1225 c.c.).

creditor_contributed.description: The creditor contributed to causing the event/damage.

creditor_failed_to_mitigate.description: The creditor failed to mitigate avoidable damage (art. 1227 c.c.).

quantification_uncertain.description: Damage quantification is uncertain or speculative.

competence_or_procedure_regular.description: The authority was competent and the procedure was regular.

motivation_is_sufficient.description: The administrative act has sufficient and coherent motivation.

participation_not_essential_or_not_denie.description: Participatory guarantees were respected, or their omission was not decisive.

silence_rule_not_applicable.description: The legal regime on procedural deadlines/silence is not applicable in this case.

vizio_non_invalidante_21_octies.description: Any procedural defect is non-invalidating under art. 21-octies L. 241/1990.

event_was_avoidable.description: The event was avoidable with ordinary diligence.

event_was_foreseeable.description: The event was foreseeable; it is not fortuitous.

risk_was_assumed_or_controllable.description: The risk was assumed or controllable, so not fortuitous.

breach_not_grave_or_not_essential.description: Breach seriousness may be contested, or essential-term effects may be limited by subsequent conduct, without denying fixed facts.

exceptio_non_rite_adimpleti.description: Counterparty suspension may be disproportionate under reciprocal-performance rules.

caparra_limits_remedies.description: Caparra remedy may absorb or limit overlap with further damages.

requires_any: The claim explicitly involves caparra confirmatoria or caparra penitenziale as a remedy or contractual clause.

penalty_excessive_or_exclusive.description: Penalty may be equitably reduced and can limit additional compensation.

further_damage_not_proven_or_not_direct.description: Further damages are not adequately proven as direct/immediate consequences.

defects_not_proven_or_not_hidden.description: Defects are not sufficiently proven or were not hidden/relevant defects.

notice_or_limitation_bar_for_vices.description: Notice timing or limitation terms may bar vices remedies.

misuse_or_external_cause_of_defect.description: Performance drop may derive from use/maintenance context, not intrinsic defect only.

remedy_reduction_preferred_over_resoluti.description: Price reduction may be more proportionate than contract termination.

consequential_damage_not_proven.description: Consequential losses are uncertain, indirect, or insufficiently documented.

custodianship_or_control_not_proven.description: Custody/control over the damage source is not clearly established.

fortuitous_external_factor.description: An external fortuitous factor may reduce or exclude objective liability.

contributory_fault_of_victim.description: Victim contribution may reduce recoverable damages.

causal_link_between_thing_and_damage_unc.description: Causal nexus between thing/animal and damage is not sufficiently proven.

internal_recourse_separate_from_external.description: Internal recourse allocation differs from external liability toward the victim.

legal_qualification_more_specific_or_alt.description: A different or more specific offence qualification may be more coherent.

subjective_element_not_fully_proven.description: Intent/culpability threshold is not fully supported by available elements.

restitution_or_reparation_reduces_penalt.description: Post-fact restitution/reparation can impact treatment of punishment.

aggravating_elements_not_fully_proven.description: Aggravating circumstances are not integrally proven.

intent_to_profit_or_unjust_gain_not_prov.description: Intent to profit/unjust gain is not sufficiently demonstrated.

exercise_of_right_or_justification_possi.description: Possible exercise-of-right/justification profile requires careful balancing.

factual_matrix_supports_lesser_offence.description: Fact pattern may support a less severe offence qualification.

publicity_or_diffusion_element_not_prove.description: Public diffusion/publicity element may be weaker than alleged.

truth_interest_continence_balance.description: Truth, public interest, and continence criteria may justify expression.

private_self_help_limits_need_precise_as.description: Limits of private self-help require strict offence-boundary assessment.

emergency_context_reduces_blameworthines.description: Emergency context may reduce reproachability and degree of fault.

foreseeability_threshold_not_met_with_ce.description: Foreseeability threshold may not be reached with sufficient certainty.

cooperative_fault_not_individualized.description: Individual contribution in cooperative negligence is not sufficiently individualized.

aggravating_circumstances_not_integrated.description: Aggravating circumstances may not be concretely integrated.

sanction_must_consider_article_133_balan.description: Sanction must be balanced under proportional criteria of article 133 c.p.

current_public_interest_not_specific.description: Current public interest for autotutela is generic or not specifically motivated.

legitimate_reliance_not_balanced.description: Legitimate private reliance has not been adequately balanced.

participation_in_autotutela_inadequate.description: Participation guarantees in autotutela phase were insufficient.

revocation_requires_indemnity_assessment.description: Revocation requires proper assessment of possible indemnity.

annulment_timing_unreasonable.description: Timing of annulment appears unreasonable relative to certainty/reliance.

delay_not_attributable_to_authority.description: Procedural delay may not be fully attributable to administrative fault.

causal_damage_from_delay_not_proven.description: Causal damage from delay is not sufficiently proven/documented.

substitute_power_not_activated.description: Substitute power route was not activated before claiming full liability.

silent_regime_specific_not_triggered.description: Specific silence regime may not be triggered in the concrete procedure.

compensation_requires_strict_proof.description: Compensation for delay requires strict proof of fault, damage, and causal nexus.

criminal_and_civil_tracks_are_distinct.description: Criminal and civil tracks remain distinct in standards and effects.

criminal_threshold_not_equal_civil_thres.description: Criminal proof threshold does not coincide with civil liability threshold.

civil_remedy_requires_autonomous_proof.description: Civil remedies require autonomous proof beyond criminal allegation alone.

damages_scope_limited_to_proven_items.description: Damages must be limited to concretely proven and causally linked items.

no_automatic_prejudice_from_criminal_all.description: No automatic civil prejudice arises from criminal allegations per se.

counter_attack_selection.step_2_optional_intersection: If theory_id is provided, intersect with theories[].default_counter_attacks when intersection is non-empty; otherwise keep full pool
counter_attack_selection.step_3_choose_k: Select 2-3 attack_ids from resulting pool based only on claim content (or fewer if pool size < 2)
counter_attack_selection.step_4_assign_per_step: Planner must assign one selected attack_id to each reasoning step

reasoner_retrieval.note: Anchor norms (core/accessory) come from the config; retrieval adds substantive norms relevant to the claim.

counter_retrieval.note: The counter only sees the claim + labels and receives contrary/neutral retrieval; it never receives the reasoner's argumentation.

router_output.causal_type_id: PEN_FACTUAL | PEN_INTERVENING | PEN_PROPERTY_QUALIFICATION | PEN_RIGHTS_BALANCING | PEN_COLPA_GRADATION | CIV_REMOTENESS | CIV_CONTRACT_REMEDIES | CIV_SALE_DEFECTS | CIV_CUSTODY_DAMAGE | AMM_PROCEDURAL_LEGITIMACY | AMM_AUTOTUTELA_BALANCE | AMM_DELAY_REMEDIES | IMPUTATION_FILTER | MIXED_PEN_CIV_CONCURRENCE

counter_output_minimal.counter_argument: string (standalone paragraph, does not reference reasoner)
